correctness.rationale: The prime-power inverse identity and Jordan multiplicativity give an exhaustive three-way split. A prime cube forces F=J+3>4^k+3. Squarefree composites with even or odd prime count have explicit product bounds >4^k+3 in absolute value. Cube-free nonsquarefree inputs ab^2 have exact bracket; even omega(a) is positive and minimized uniquely at a=1,b=2; odd omega(a) is bounded using A/B<zeta(2)^2/zeta(4)=5/2, with separate strict b=2 and b>=3 estimates. The equalizing input n=4 evaluates to 4^k+3. Independently computed convolution inverse confirms exact finite cases k=2..8,n<=10000, which is corroboration rather than infinite proof.

value.rationale: The extremum is taken over all composites, with every permitted k, for a newly studied prime-characterizing arithmetic function. The exact distance of the nearest composite to zero is canonically motivated by the detector and the stability of exact zero identification under bounded numerical perturbations. The unique minimizer n=4 and its exponentially growing sharp gap are neither arbitrary cutoffs nor a mere restatement of nonvanishing; no algorithmic efficiency claim is made.
